thread:
Alex: Heads-up — opening a docs PR to add compact fallback examples for 429s/timeouts across JS + Python SDKs. Need canonical snippets and a couple of anchor/link fixes. @Tess can you pair on the Python examples?
Tess: On it. Any preference for pattern? `Retry-After` handling vs client-side exponential backoff with jitter?
Alex: Prefer exponential backoff + jitter as the main pattern, and a short example showing model-swap fallback (e.g. fallback to a smaller context model). Also include a tiny note about trimming context.
Mike: I can pick up the JS snippet and a tiny browser advisory. Where should we link the examples — err-ref page or the runbook?
Sophia: Both. Err-ref for developer-facing examples and the runbook for ops playbook. I'll add anchors for `429` and `timeout` headings so we can link directly.
deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789 (staging preview attached)
Tess: Draft Python snippet idea:
```python
import time
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RateLimitError
client = RedwoodClient()
for attempt in range(5):
    try:
        resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=512)
        break
    except RateLimitError as e:
        time.sleep(backoff_with_jitter(attempt))
else:
    # fallback to smaller model or trim context
    resp = client.generate(prompt_trimmed, model='redwood-small')
```
We should annotate `backoff_with_jitter` and show a tiny helper. Also mention `Retry-After` header when present.
Mike: JS snippet (short):
```js
await withRetry(() => client.chat.create({model: 'redwood-pro', messages}), {retries: 4, jitter: true})
// if still failing: swap to 'redwood-lite' and log the reason
```
I'll make the API call match our SDK surface in the PR.
Alex: Two editorial asks: 1) add a `doc:429-examples` metrics tag in examples so we can track usage, 2) add a 1-line callout about server-side timeouts (`request.timeout = 10s`) and how that maps to SDK-level `TimeoutError`.
Sophia: I'll update the err-ref TOC + add the anchors. Also will add a short paragraph in the runbook about choosing between trimming context vs model swap (and include cost tradeoffs).
Emily: @Alex @Tess @Mike — assigning reviewers: Alex (author), Tess (Python + prose), Mike (JS + browser note), Sophia (TOC/anchors). Target to merge by EOD Friday.
Tess: :thumbsup: I can review the Python snippet and the prose. Also will add a short example showing parsing `Retry-After` header: `wait = int(resp.headers.get('Retry-After', 0))`.
Mike: I'll add a brief browser compatibility note (CORS/credential advice) and a tiny example that avoids blocking the UI thread.
Alex: Thanks all. Quick ask — keep code blocks concise (no huge multi-file examples). I'll squash/fixup commits and mark the PR `ready for review` when done. Ping here for last-minute nits.
Tess: soundsgood :+1:
Sophia: will check anchors after the PR lands.
Alex: Great, merging plan looks good. If anything blocks, drop it here and we'll reroute.
